summary: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held academic posts at Hokkaido University, Tohoku University, and Toyo Bunko.

Kiyozo Kazama specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Takatsu, and at the University of Vienna. He held teaching posts at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.

Indologist Klaus Bruhn studied at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring, completing his doctorate and habilitation. He later served as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991/1996.

Klaus Butzenberger works in Indology, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned his master's at the University of Munich and pursued doctoral studies under Friedrich Wilhelm. He held academic positions at Munich, Freie Universität Berlin, Humboldt University, and the University of Tübingen.

Klaus Karttunen works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto, Asko Parpola, Henrik Zilliacus, Holger Thesleff, and Maarit Kaimio. He held appointments at the University of Helsinki, the Academy of Finland, and Freiburg.

Klaus Ludwig Janert specialized in Indology. He studied at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg, Goethe University Frankfurt under Paul Thieme, and the University of Tübingen. He later held posts at the University of Göttingen and the University of Cologne.

Klaus Mylius worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Leipzig. His teaching posts included Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, Bayreuth, the University of Göttingen, and Goethe University Frankfurt.

Klaus Pinte is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served on the postdoctoral teaching staff at Ghent University in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn works in Iranian/Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Hamburg (under Bertold Spuler, Wolfgang Lentz, and Annemarie von Gabain), and Giessen. He held posts at Giessen, Göttingen Academy of Sciences, and Göttingen University.
Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied under Paul Hacker. He held a post as Dozent Dr. at the University of Münster, attested in 1978.

Klaus Wille is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as holding academic and research positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1997 and at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities between 2000 and 2026.

Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Klaus Sagaster, Michael Hahn at the University of Marburg, and Tibetan masters, habilitating at Hamburg. He held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, Hamburg, and the University of Vienna.

Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Philosophisch-Theologische Hochschule Benediktbeuern and earned a Doctor theologiae from the University of Munich, where he served as a Lehrbeauftragter in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under Peter Schalk and received his Doctor of Philosophy from Uppsala University in 2000.

Knut A. Jacobsen works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held professorships at the University of Bergen starting in 1996 and at the University of Oslo from approximately 1996 to 1999.

Kobun Otogawa was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, and Eihei-ji. He also trained under Kodo Sawaki and held posts at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center, Haiku Zendo, and Naropa University.

Kodai Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership roles at Komazawa University, including president, and lectured at the University of Tokyo.
Kodo Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his master's and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1966 to 2004.

Kodo Sawaki specialized in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Takada College, Senju-ji, Horyu-ji, and under Koho Sawada, Zenko Sawada, Ryoun Fueoka, Join Saeki, and Sotan Oka. He held posts at Komazawa University and Antai-ji.
Kodo Yamada was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He taught at both Komazawa University and Keio University.
